title: Rumack-Matthew Nomogram: Assessing Toxicity

items.text: How to use: draw a level at 4 hours or later after a single acute ingestion and plot it against time since ingestion.
items.md: **How to use:**  draw a level at 4 hours or later after a single acute ingestion and plot it against time since ingestion.

items.text: Above the treatment line: give NAC.
Limits: not valid before 4 hours, for unknown ingestion time, staggered or repeated supratherapeutic ingestion, or chronic use; treat these using clinical judgment, AST/ALT and poison control.
items.md: **Limits:**  not valid before 4 hours, for unknown ingestion time, staggered or repeated supratherapeutic ingestion, or chronic use; treat these using clinical judgment, AST/ALT and poison control.

items.text: Example: 8 h, 120 mcg/mL is above the line, so start NAC.
items.md: Example: 8 h, 120 mcg/mL is above the line, so start NAC.

notes:
The nomogram predicts hepatotoxicity risk after a single acute ingestion; if time of ingestion is unknown or ingestion is chronic, do not rely on it. Start NAC without waiting if presentation is late or the level is unavailable and ingestion is significant.

After 24 hours the nomogram is not used: 4.7 mcg/mL is only where the treatment line ends, not a safe cutoff. Get AST/ALT; a detectable level or elevated AST/ALT guides NAC, per protocol or poison control.

Know: Use the Rumack-Matthew nomogram.
